    Bake epidemiological recipe features with explicit history

    Source: R/recipes-history.R
    epi_bake_history.Rd

    Prep a recipe on training data first. This helper prepends the supplied raw history to the new data, bakes the combined series, and returns only the new rows. This allows the package's lag, rolling and exposure steps to see prior rows at the training/assessment boundary. The helper accepts only a trained recipe whose steps are step_epi_lags(), step_epi_rolling(), step_epi_rates(), or step_epi_exposure_window(), with skip = FALSE. Other recipe steps are rejected because arbitrary steps may alter row order or have different semantics when history is prepended. The two data frames must have identical column names, represent a single time series, and be strictly sorted; all history times must precede all new times. Time units need not be equally spaced, but lag and window sizes count rows, not elapsed time. The caller must provide enough raw history for all chained steps.

    Usage

    epi_bake_history(.data, recipe, history, time)

    Arguments

    .data

    An ungrouped, non-empty data frame of new rows for one series.

    recipe

    A prepped recipes recipe containing only the supported steps.

    history

    An ungrouped, non-empty data frame of earlier raw observations with the same columns as .data.

    time

    A single numeric or whole-day Date time column, present in both datasets and strictly increasing within each.

    Value

    A tibble containing only the baked new rows.

    Details

    This does not alter or store history in a recipe. The recipe must have been prepped without access to future data. step_epi_rolling() and step_epi_exposure_window() include the current row; they leak information if applied to a target value unavailable at prediction time. Later new rows can also use earlier new-row observations, so a multi-step forecast made all at once must not supply outcomes that would not yet be observed. For grouped series call separately for each group. Row identity is verified through validation of supported steps and the baked row count.

    Examples

    d <- data.frame(day = 1:6, cases = 1:6)
rec <- recipes::recipe(~., data = d[1:4, ]) |> step_epi_lags(cases, lag = 1)
prepped <- recipes::prep(rec)
epi_bake_history(d[5:6, ], prepped, history = d[1:4, ], time = day)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>     day cases lag1_cases
#>   <int> <int>      <int>
#> 1     5     5          4
#> 2     6     6          5
